theirs.title: Published by the town, the district and the state
theirs.blurb: Primary documents. We did not write any of these and we did not commission them. 25 came from the Town by records request and say so on their row; one more was handed over by somebody acting in a town role, and they are named on its row; the rest were already public. 38 of them link back to the exact file the publisher put up, and 28 of those addresses have been checked the only way an address can be — by downloading what is there now and matching it against our copy, byte for byte. A link that merely looks right is not a source. 18 still have no address of their own, and they are three different things: state reports built on form submission, where the page and the jurisdiction are the whole answer; a table we built here from a document that is itself listed above; and documents gathered before the mirror existed, where nobody wrote down where they came from. Only the last is a gap, it is a gap on our side and not the town’s, and it is named in notes/findings/DATA-WANTED.md. Where a document is unreadable or says something inconvenient, it is here anyway.

reference.title: Everything else the district and the town publish
reference.blurb: Mirrored here so it is available and so no figure has to be looked up over the network. 271 of these 286 feed no number on this site. The other 15 are byte-identical copies of primary sources listed above — kept, and marked as such on their row, because a mirror with the load-bearing documents quietly removed is no longer a copy of the publisher’s page. It is all here because a document nobody kept is a document nobody can check, and because we would rather hold what we did not use than be asked why we did not look.

ours.title: Written by this project, not by the town
ours.blurb: Everything below this line is ours. It is not town information, it carries no official standing, and nobody at the district or the Town has reviewed or approved it. It is one resident’s reading of the documents above, published so it can be argued with — which means checked against those documents, and disagreed with where the reading is wrong.
